subject: english-literature

items.q: Should a play be analysed exactly like a novel?
items.correct: No — drama is written to be performed, so stagecraft matters.
items.misconception: Yes, plays and novels are analysed identically.
items.why: Consider staging, dramatic devices and the effect on an audience.

items.correct: When the audience knows something a character does not.
items.misconception: A surprising coincidence in the plot.
items.random_wrong: When two characters argue on stage.
items.why: Dramatic irony builds tension because the audience is ahead of a character.

items.q: How should context be used when studying a play?
items.correct: Woven in to illuminate how it shapes the play's meaning.
items.random_wrong: Ignored, since only the words matter.
items.why: Link context to meaning and audience response.
